scenario.name: Red Hat, CISA & MITRE DFIR — Linux auditd SSH authorized_keys & PAM Module Persistence Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a Linux vault protected by two distinct door-check systems: a personal spare-key ring hanging inside each employee locker and a central badge-verification office handling every login attempt. An intruder quietly slips their own public key onto an employee spare-key ring and attempts to swap a rigged verification module into the central badge office, while kernel file watches, package integrity seals, and login fingerprint logs stitch together an airtight attribution trail. In this scenario (T1098.004, Red Hat, CISA & MITRE DFIR, Linux auditd SSH authorized_keys & PAM Module Persistence Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: linux Auditd File-Watch Trigger, then pAM Shared Library Modification Detection, then correlating /var/log/secure Accepted. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Linux Auditd File-Watch Trigger, then PAM Shared Library Modification Detection, then Correlating /var/log/secure Accepted, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 257 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Linux Auditd File-Watch Trigger on ~/.ssh/authorized_keys Modification (SYSCALL openat)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1098.004 - Account Manipulation: SSH Authorized Keys)
stages.description: To guarantee silent passwordless entry even if user passwords change, the intruder appends their own public key straight onto the target user authorized-keys sheet, instantly tripping the kernel file-watch sensor bolted onto that sheet. When a compromised service process modifies /root/.ssh/authorized_keys with the O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_APPEND flags, the Linux kernel audit subsystem (configured with -w /root/.ssh -p wa -k ssh_persistence) emits correlated SYSCALL, CWD, and PATH records in /var/log/audit/audit.log capturing the exact process (exe), login UID (auid), effective UID (euid), and inode number (logged in Linux Audit Event 257 with AuditKey=ssh_persistence, Syscall=257 , sys_openat with O_WRONLY|O_APPEND, AuditLoginUid=auid=1001 , Pivoted User -> euid=0 , root, ModifiedPath=/root/.ssh/authorized_keys , inode 1310942 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1556.003 - Modify Authentication Process: Pluggable Authentication Modules)
